title: Regionless failover simulator + Terraform plan validator for Private VPC drills
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable 'regionless' failover simulator and a Terraform plan validator that can run against private VPC deployments to validate multi-region DR drills without impacting production workloads. The simulator will exercise routing, KV lock fencing, prefix cache replay, and upgrade canaries. The Terraform plan validator will run a dry-run against IaC modules to detect potential cross-region resource drift, dangerous plan actions (delete_create for stateful resources), and provider version mismatches before a drill is executed.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can emulate traffic routing shifts between two private regions without changing live DNS records
Terraform plan validator flags any stateful resource recreation and surfaces recommended mitigation steps
Automated preflight completes in <10 minutes and produces a signed artifact pushed to S3 for audit
Runbook snippets and failure-mode playbooks added to the DR runbook and reviewed by SRE and Security
Successful dry-run drill executed in staging with KV fence test and automatic rollback on unsafe plan
steps: Spike: prototype traffic shim that redirects a percentage of traffic to backup region (done)
Implement KV fencing harness and idempotent promotion script
Author Terraform plan validator module that wraps 'terraform plan' and runs custom checks
Integrate plan validator into CircleCI pipeline and provide a dry-run report artifact
Add canary upgrade flow: kick a single replica in backup region and validate model compatibility
Wire simulator to Console dashboard to surface preflight results and run history
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed — prototype shim uses iptables nat + Envoy routing in a test VPC to simulate region handoff. Observed cache warmup latency ~300ms worst-case.
2026-03-06: Design review with SRE and PM — decided to favour a non-intrusive 'regionless' mode that only simulates routing and state-change signals, not DNS updates.
2026-03-09: Terraform validator PoC flags provider downgrades and resource recreation heuristics. Initial false-positive on ephemeral LB replacement addressed.
2026-03-12: PR opened for terraform-module (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321). CI now produces plan artifacts to s3://redwood-dr-dryruns/staging/ENG-91321/
2026-03-13: Scheduled first staging drill 2026-03-22. Added canary promotion + KV fence test to runbook. Noted need for SSO artifact signing for audit.
runbook_snippets:
# preflight validate
echo "Starting DR preflight" && ./tools/terraform-validator --plan s3://redwood-dr-dryruns/plan.json --policy checks/policy.yaml

# kv fence check
python tools/kv_fence_test.py --region us-west-2 --backup-region eu-west-1 --threshold 500

# canary promotion
kubectl annotate deployment/redwood-inference-serving promote-canary=true --namespace production
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Chose regionless simulation over DNS cutover to avoid customer-visible churn during rehearsals
Opted for Terraform plan validator with policy hooks vs. full stateful simulation due to cost and complexity
Will keep canary promotions limited to non-critical model pools during initial rollout to reduce blast radius
review_feedback: 2026-03-07 from Priya Mehta (SRE): add KV fence timeout alarms and increase preflight timeout to 15m
2026-03-10 from Marco Liu (Security): require signed dry-run artifacts and retention for 90 days
2026-03-12 from Elena Grigorev (PM): add clear acceptance criteria for Terraform 'no-op' validation
estimated_cost_impact: approx $350/month extra run cost for dry-run artifacts in S3 and staging infra
next_actions: Merge terraform validator PR and publish module to internal registry
Run the staging drill with SRE shepherding and collect telemetry
Iterate on policy rules to reduce false positives and add provider-version pinning checks
